title: From next-token prediction to tool proposals
notes: 3 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Language is an interface, not an oracle. Define: Generate a proposal, then verify the claim outside the model. title: A token is not necessarily a word
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: A token is not necessarily a word. Define: A tokenizer maps text to integer IDs using a specified vocabulary. Walk through: Character demo: hot = h,o,t; a production subword tokenizer can split differently. Preserve tokenizer identity. Ask: Can one word always be counted as one token? Expected answer and boundary: No. Token boundaries depend on the tokenizer and text. The notebook uses characters, not a production LLM tokenizer. Visual purpose: show Text > Token boundaries > Integer IDs > Context sequence. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. title: Autoregression factorizes a sequence
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Autoregression factorizes a sequence. Define: Each conditional distribution uses the preceding context only. Walk through: p(A)=0.5; p(B given A)=0.6; p(C given AB)=0.2; joint probability=0.06. Ask: Does the factorization prove the sequence is true? Expected answer and boundary: No. It describes sequence probability under a model, not truth. The multiplication follows the chain rule. Visual purpose: show p(x1...xT) = product p(xt given x before t). Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. Transition: connect this checked mechanism to the next beat; preserve the lab artifact where requested. title: Cross-entropy penalizes surprise
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Cross-entropy penalizes surprise. Define: Training lowers negative log probability on observed next tokens. Walk through: If p=0.8 then -ln(p)=0.223; if p=0.2 then loss=1.609. Mean=0.916 nats. Ask: Why is assigning low probability to the observed token costly? Expected answer and boundary: Negative log grows as probability approaches zero. Mean teacher-forced loss is not factual verification. Visual purpose: show Observed token > Predicted probability > Negative log > Mean loss. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. Transition: connect this checked mechanism to the next beat; preserve the lab artifact where requested. title: Attention selects context-dependent mixtures
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Attention selects context-dependent mixtures. Define: Causal masking prevents a position from reading later tokens. Walk through: At position 2, keys 1 and 2 are allowed; keys 3 and 4 are blocked before softmax. Ask: Does attention provide an external source of facts? Expected answer and boundary: No. It mixes representations from supplied context. Retrieved evidence and its quality remain separate responsibilities. Visual purpose: show QK transpose / sqrt(dk) > Causal mask > Row softmax > Weighted V. title: Sampling changes a distribution
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Sampling changes a distribution. Define: Temperature divides logits before softmax; it is not a truth control. Walk through: Logits [2,0]: T=1 gives [0.881,0.119]; T=2 gives [0.731,0.269]. Ask: What does increasing temperature change here? Expected answer and boundary: It flattens this distribution and raises the lower-logit token probability. It does not make the content more or less factual by definition. Visual purpose: show Logits > Divide by T > Softmax > Sample. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. Transition: connect this checked mechanism to the next beat; preserve the lab artifact where requested. title: A tiny language model is inspectable
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: A tiny language model is inspectable. Define: Character bigrams estimate the next character from one previous character. Walk through: Run the fixed original teaching corpus. Find the most frequent successor of a space and compare its count with its probability. Ask: Is this a miniature Transformer? Expected answer and boundary: No. It is a trained conditional-count language model with one-character context; it lacks attention and contextual embeddings. Visual purpose: show Training text > Transition counts > Add-one smoothing > Next-character probabilities. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. Transition: connect this checked mechanism to the next beat; preserve the lab artifact where requested. title: Prediction before sampling creates evidence

Walk through: Predict whether lower temperature concentrates probabilities; compare entropy and sampled continuations without changing the corpus. Ask: Must a lower-entropy model produce a better answer? Expected answer and boundary: No. Entropy measures distribution concentration.
